Sysvar slot-hash account read, update, encode, and memory management functions.

# Purpose
This C file implements the `slot_hashes` sysvar for the bank state. It provides functions to create, join, leave, delete, read, write, and update the `fd_slot_hashes_global_t` data structure that stores recent slot and hash pairs. The code uses the account database and transaction context to load the sysvar account from `funk`, decode its binary form, update the entry for the parent slot, and write the updated data back into the sysvar account with `fd_sysvar_account_update`.

The main update path is [`fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_update`](<#fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_update>). It reads the current sysvar state, creates a new one if the account does not exist, scans the deque of `fd_slot_hash_t` entries, and replaces the hash for the current parent slot when it finds a match. If no match exists, it inserts a new entry at the head of the deque and removes the tail entry when the deque is full. The file also defines memory layout helpers such as [`fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_footprint`](<#fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_footprint>), [`fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_new`](<#fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_new>), [`fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_join`](<#fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_join>), and [`fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_delete`](<#fd_sysvar_slot_hashes_delete>), which manage aligned shared memory for the global object and its internal deque.
